title: Naturally Occurring GMOs Explained
reason: Discusses the natural occurrence of genetic modification through microbes and how this process is similar to modern GMO techniques.

tasks.task: Explain how natural processes involving microbes led to understanding genetic modification in plants.

subtasks.text: Point out that microbes were cutting and pasting DNA into plants long before lab-based genetic modification.
Describe the crown gall condition as an example of natural genetic modification.
Explain the mechanism by which microbes insert DNA into plant cells.
Describe the first step in modern microbial gene insertion technique—the solution preparation.
Note that the process for crop plants is similar to the simpler one used for flowers.

tasks.task: Highlight the historical and contemporary natural occurrence of GMO-like processes.

subtasks.text: Mention that DNA from the same microbes has been present in sweet potatoes for 9,000 years.
Emphasize that all sweet potatoes, even certified organic ones, contain microbial DNA.
